subject: Storage nomenclature & retention paths — request vs answer Q&A
messages:

Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>

Subject: Clarify default retention for 'request' vs 'answer' (procurement)

Hi Tessa,

Hope you're well. Procurement at BrightBank has flagged a couple of items in our contract draft that need clear definitions before we sign: in particular, the default retention periods and the canonical names you use in documentation for "request" vs "answer" (we've seen different terms across pages).

Two asks from legal/procurement:
- A short, plain-English description of what Redwood stores by default (e.g., user input, streamed fragments, final generated outputs) and the default retention window for each.
- The exact naming you use in APIs/logs so our engineers can map to our data classification (e.g., is "request" called "input" or "user_text", is "answer" "model_output" or "generated_text").

If possible could you provide a one-page summary we can attach to the SOW and a single spreadsheet matrix? Procurement needs this by EOD Thursday to stay on schedule.

Thanks — we appreciate the quick turnaround.

Emily

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify default retention for 'request' vs 'answer' (procurement)

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Kimberly (security & compliance) and Karthik (product/policy) to confirm language. Below is an initial, concise mapping we use internally — I kept it intentionally literal so you can paste into the SOW: 

- Canonical naming (how we refer to items in logs/docs):
  • request / user_input / input_text — the raw user-provided content sent in an API request (text, prompt fields, attachment metadata).
  • streamed_fragment — partial tokens/frames emitted during a streaming session before the finalization call; used for debugging and stream reconstruction.
  • final_output / generated_output / model_answer — the finalized answer returned to the caller (post-processing applied).
  • derivatives / embeddings / vector_index_entries — indexable outputs derived from model responses (separate retention rules).

- Default retention windows (hosted API):
  • request (user_input): 45 days (default) — kept to support debugging, analytics, and quality monitoring.
  • streamed_fragment: 7 days (default) — short-lived buffer for stream replay and troubleshooting; auto-pruned.
  • final_output (generated_output): 90 days (default) — retained for auditability, tracing regressions, and customer support.
  • derivatives/embeddings: configurable per-customer; default retention 365 days unless customer opts out.

Notes/constraints:
- Customers can request shorter retention or immediate purge via the account settings or by raising a deletion/erasure request with our support flow (see Kimberly's note below for evidence/turnaround).
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, retention is configurable and governed by the customer's config and contractual terms; the above defaults apply to hosted customers only.

I'll attach a one-page summary and a simple retention matrix shortly. Kimberly/Karthik — please flag any legal precision we should swap in.

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan

Subject: Re: Clarify default retention for 'request' vs 'answer' (procurement)

Emily / Team —

Thanks, Tessa. A few small edits for contractual clarity and the exact process for erasure/evidence:

1) Precise language for SOW (recommended):
  - ""Request (user_input)" refers to the original user-provided content transmitted to Redwood's inference API (including prompt fields and attachment metadata). Redwood retains request records for 45 days by default for hosted customers, unless otherwise agreed in writing.""
  - ""Final output (generated_output)" refers to the completed model response returned to the caller after any configured post-processing. Redwood retains final outputs for 90 days by default for hosted customers, unless otherwise agreed in writing.""

2) Erasure / deletion process (short version):
  - Customer initiates erasure by filing a support request (submitter must provide account id and a date/time range or message IDs).
  - Redwood confirms scope within 48 hours and begins background erasure; most standard hosted erasure requests complete within 5 business days.
  - Redwood can provide proof of deletion for compliance audits (hashes removed, deletion timestamps) subject to a data-disclosure addendum.

3) Streaming fragments: described as ephemeral (7-day buffer) and not included in standard audit exports unless customers enable session-tracing.

I've also exported a retention matrix for your procurement team (attached). If you need wording tightened further for legal, happy to provide a short clause with defined terms.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
(attachment: retention_matrix_v1.xlsx, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Tessa / Kimberly —

This is great, thank you both. Procurement would like the one-page PDF and the spreadsheet as separate attachments in our packet; Kimberly's suggested SOW wording looks good and is what our legal expects. Two quick follow-ups: 

1) Can you confirm whether the 45/90 windows are measured from ingestion timestamp or from the last read by the customer? (we assume ingestion, but need confirmation)
2) For the erasure turnaround: if we include a clause that requires completion within 3 business days, is that something Redwood is willing to contractually accept for enterprise customers? If not, can we get a statement of typical completion SLA and any upgrade path (e.g., accelerated erasure for Dedicated accounts)?

If it's easier I'll take these as short bullets and add them to the SOW draft.

Thanks again — we should be on track to finalize next week pending this detail.

Emily
